facts.title: tomato and corn pie
ingredients: 6 tablespoons (3 ounces or 85 grams) cold unsalted butter, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
1 1/2 cups corn (from about 3 ears), coarsely chopped by hand or lightly puréed in a food processor, divided
1 3/4 cups (7 ounces or 200 grams) coarsely grated sharp cheddar cheese, divided
facts.author: Deb Perelman

steps.text: Make the crust: Whisk together flour, baking powder, and 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt in a bowl, then blend in cold butter with your fingertips or a pastry blender until it resembles coarse meal. Add milk, stirring until mixture just forms a dough, then gather into a ball.

Divide dough in half and roll out one piece on a well-floured counter (my preference) or between two sheets of plastic wrap (the original recipe’s suggestion, but I imagined it would annoyingly stick to the plastic) into a 12-inch round (1/8 inch thick). Either fold the round gently in quarters, lift it into a 9-inch pie plate and gently unfold and center it or, if you’re using the plastic warp method, remove top sheet of plastic wrap, then lift dough using bottom sheet of plastic wrap and invert into pie plate. Pat the dough in with your fingers trim any overhang beyond 1/2-inch of dough.

Assemble the pie: Preheat oven to 400°F with rack in middle. If your kitchen is excessively warm, as ours is, go ahead and put the second half of the dough in the fridge until you’re ready to use it. Whisk together mayonnaise and lemon juice.

If you’d like to peel your tomatoes (I no longer do this): Cut an X in bottom of each tomato and blanch in a large pot of boiling water 10 seconds. Immediately transfer with a slotted spoon to an ice bath to cool. Peel tomatoes.
To seed your tomatoes (please do this, it reduces wetness): Cut tomatoes in half crosswise and use a spoon or your fingers to remove as many seeds as you can from each half.

Both methods: Slice tomatoes crosswise 1/4-inch thick. Arrange half of tomatoes in crust, overlapping, and sprinkle with half of corn, half of herbs, salt, pepper, and cheese. Repeat layering with remaining tomatoes, corn, basil, chives, salt, and pepper. Pour lemon mayonnaise over filling and sprinkle with remaining cheese.

Roll out remaining piece of dough into a 12-inch round in same manner, then fit over filling, folding overhang under edge of bottom crust and pinching edge to seal. Cut 4 steam vents in top crust and brush crust with melted butter (2 teaspoons).
Bake: Bake pie until crust is golden and filling is bubbling, 30 to 35 minutes, then cool on a rack.
Serve: Warm or at room temperature.

An idea: Want to slab pie this and serve it to a crowd? I agree, it would be brilliant. This is how I’d approach it: Make 1 1/2 batches of the crust (slab pies require more crust for the same amount of filling) and arrange the filling in one layer instead of two in a parchment-lined 15x10x1-inch pan. Increase the amount of butter you brush the top with to a tablespoon or two and the baking time to about 45 minutes (this is an estimate, you should take it out when it is golden and the filling is bubbling). Be sure to remove the tomato seeds; that extra wetness could make for a slab pie mess.

notes: Do ahead: Pie can be baked 1 day ahead and chilled. Reheat in a 350°F oven until warm, about 30 minutes.

A few gentle 2026 updates: These days, I use half to none of the basil and double the chives. I never peel the tomatoes anymore; the skins do not bother me. The original recipe had you seed your tomatoes after slicing them but I found this very finicky. It’s easier to scoop seeds out when tomatoes are halved. If you eat it on the first day, there’s still a bit of wetness, however, just less so. I find that overnight in the fridge, it sets up nicely if you’re planning ahead. Note: I’ve got a tomato and corn cobbler, a biscuit-topped casserole inspired by this pie, in Smitten Kitchen Keepers and I know you’d love it.
